title: Active nematic rods from noise whose self-made surfactant ring does work: it holds the fuel of their own active stress, persists through fission into both daughters, and nearly triples division (SIBD; motility only on 1 of 3 seeds)
summary: c11's ringed active-nematic rods (20261025T1141) made functional: the active stress is zeta g(f) Q with g = f/(f+3), and f is a fuel the rods make (kf ((1+phi)/2)^4), that decays and diffuses with permeability Df/(1+5 (s/0.45)^12), so only the adsorbed ring of surfactant s blocks it. On 3/3 seeds rods form from noise and every body carries a closed s ring at its interface (interface score: 100% of 28-96 bodies membrane-like, median rim/core 3.2, rim/outside 4.0-4.7; ringstat.txt); the ring pinches into a figure-8 at fission and each daughter leaves with its own closed ring (fission_strips_*.png). The ring holds core fuel at 0.58-0.59 vs 0.35 without it, and the colony makes 14/5/11 persistent splits (generation 3/3/3) vs 5/2/7 (generation 2/1/2) when chi_s=0 smears s into a fill (0% membrane-like), and 5 (generation 1) on seed 0 when the ring is present but does not gate (beta=0). The linear twin (CH replaced by diffusion at 2aM) makes no bodies at all. Raising zeta 1.8x without a ring restores division (18 splits, gen 3), so the ring acts by raising the active stress inside the rods. dt/2 on seed 0: 12 splits, gen 3, 100% ringed.

claims.statement: On 3/3 seeds (128^2, T=1000), rods that nucleate from a uniform state plus noise each carry a closed ring of a surfactant they make (interface rim/core 3.2, rim/outside 4.0; 100% of bodies), and the ring does work: it holds the fuel that powers their active stress (core f 0.58 vs 0.35 with chi_s=0 or beta=0) and with it the rods divide by binary fission into ringed daughters (persistent splits 14/5/11, generation 3 on every seed; merge/split 0.11/0/0.12) against 5/2/7, generation 2/1/2, with the ring smeared (chi_s=0) and 5, generation 1, with the ring present but not gating (beta=0).
claims.track: seed 0, labkit track 14 (pack/seed0/lineage.png): born by fission of founder track 7 at frame 60, divides at frame 123 into tracks 23 and 24; every body in this run, including 14 and its daughters, is ring-bounded (ringstat.txt, 96/96); fission_strips_seed0.png shows the ring dividing with the body

controls_run.B: pack_chis0/seed0-2 (chi_s=0: ring smeared, 0% membrane-like, core fuel 0.35, fewer splits) and pack_beta0/seed0 (ring kept, gating removed: core fuel 0.35, 5 splits gen 1)
controls_run.D: pack_chis0/ and pack_beta0/ as above; pack_chis0_zeta81/seed0 (no ring, zeta x1.8: 18 splits, gen 3, showing the ring acts through the active stress)
controls_run.numerics: pack_dt2/seed0 (dt 0.025: 12 splits, gen 3, 90/90 ringed, core fuel 0.56)

claims.bd_control: pack_linear/seed0: the matched Laplacian-only twin (Cahn-Hilliard replaced by linear diffusion at the bulk CH diffusivity 2aM, all else equal) forms no bodies (0 components), so no ring, fuel or division; the world succeeds on 3/3 seeds.

limits: Motility is weak: 4.6 body lengths max on seed 0 (3.5 at dt/2) but 1.9 and 2.1 on seeds 1 and 2, so M is not claimed and C:swim-divide's SIBMD is not reached here. The ring-off arms still divide, only less (division needs activity, the ring raises it), so the ring's effect is quantitative (2-3x splits, one generation deeper), not on/off. The permeability law is steep (Hill n=12 at s=0.45) and chosen so that only the adsorbed ring gates; the containment is therefore designed, and the work it does is scored under mechanism. Rods are about 4 px wide and the ring is 1-2 px at dx=1; no resolution test yet. The labkit radial score (rho around centroids) mixes the two rails of thin rods and gives aggregate s rim/core 1.03-1.36 (14-61 of 36-97 individuals membrane-like); ringstat.py measures the interface band instead. Seed 1 nucleates only 3 founders. The linear twin fails trivially (no phase separation) and does not test the active stress.
